model_solution:
1. Main phase 1: Activate Gideon, Ally of Zendikar's +1 ability. Gideon becomes a 5/5 indestructible Human Soldier Ally creature (6/6 with the emblem) that's still a planeswalker. He has been under your control since the turn began, so he can attack.
2. Cast Illusory Wrappings (Farmland for U + 2 more mana) targeting Gideon. His base P/T becomes 0/2; with the emblem he is 1/3.
3. Cast Dead Weight (Swamp) targeting your Knight Ally token. It becomes 1/1 (2/2 base, +1/+1 emblem, -2/-2).
4. Go to combat and attack the opponent with Gideon (1/3) and the Knight Ally token (1/1). Both have skulk from Behind the Scenes and have power 1; Seraph of the Suns (4), Sparring Mummy (3), and Labyrinth Guardian (2) all have greater power, so none of them can legally block either attacker.
5. In the declare blockers step, after no blocks are declared, cast Anguished Unmaking (Farmland for W, Swamp for B, plus 1 more) targeting Illusory Wrappings, exiling it. You lose 3 life (irrelevant). Gideon reverts to 5/5, +1/+1 from the emblem = 6/6. Blocks have already been declared, so he remains unblocked.
6. Combat damage: Gideon deals 6 and the Knight Ally token deals 1, for 7 total. The opponent goes from 7 to 0 and loses.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the mana available with 4 Irrigated Farmlands and 3 Swamps, then checking the opponent's blockers and life total against our attackers—Knight Ally token, Gideon, and Behind the Scenes granting skulk to make creatures unblockable by bigger creatures.

I'm working through combos: Temmet targeting a token for +1/+1 and unblockable, weighing whether Gideon's 0 ability or +1 gives better outcomes, then considering shrinking their blockers with Dead Weight and Illusory Wrappings to get enough damage past skulk-protected attackers to close out the remaining 7 life.

Option A: Gideon +1 makes a 6/6 attacker plus a 3/3 Knight, but Mummy can just block Gideon since skulk only stops blocks from higher-power creatures. Trying Illusory Wrappings on Mummy to shrink it to 0/2 actually backfires—lowering its power just makes it eligible to block everything under skulk, so that's the wrong approach.

Instead I should focus on removing blockers outright: Dead Weight kills the Guardian for 1 mana, Anguished Unmaking handles Seraph or Mummy for 3, leaving some mana for Temmet. Or I could use Temmet's trigger to make the Knight token unblockable at 4/4, then pump Gideon to 6/6 and see how the remaining blockers stack up against that combo.

I try Behind the Scenes for +1/+1 to all, but that only gets me to 5 damage, not 7. Then I consider Illusory Wrappings on Gideon to shrink him for skulk, letting him dodge all three blockers, but his damage drops to 1, so combined with Knight it's still only 5 — not enough. Now I'm wondering if putting Illusory Wrappings on the Knight instead, combined with Temmet's buff, gets me closer to the 7 I need.

Killing off blockers seems more promising — Dead Weight on the Guardian and Anguished Unmaking on the Seraph clears two threats, using 6 of my 7 mana, but if I spend the last mana on Temmet, only one blocker remains and it can still stop Gideon, leaving me with just 4 unblocked damage from the Knight. Dropping Temmet and instead using the last 3 mana for Illusory Wrappings on the Mummy shrinks its power to zero, letting it block anything via skulk but removing its threat, which finally opens up Knight (3) plus Gideon (6) for a total of 9 damage getting through.

I keep circling back to whether skulk math works: if my attacker's power drops below all the blockers' power, nothing can block it, but that also weakens my own damage output unless I pump after blocks are declared, and none of my mana-efficient tricks let me do that at instant speed. Gideon's loyalty abilities are sorcery-speed only, so I can't boost him mid-combat, and enchanting Gideon with Illusory Wrappings after he's already a creature is another avenue worth checking.

I try putting Wrappings on Gideon to shrink him to 1/3 so skulk makes him unblockable, then use Anguished Unmaking on the aura itself after blockers are declared, restoring him to 6/6 unblocked damage — that's 6 mana total, leaving 1 for Dead Weight, but the total damage still falls short of lethal since the Knight gets blocked. I try shifting Dead Weight onto different creatures to see if any combination lets both attackers through for exactly 7, and I'm also considering swapping in Temmet as a cheaper option to free up mana.

Trying Gideon as the attacker instead: +1 makes him a 6/6, but Dead Weight brings him to 4/4, and Skulk then fails since no blocker exceeds power 4. Swapping Wrappings onto Gideon instead gives 1/3, which doesn't help either — I'm still short of the total needed.

Then I try Dead Weight on the Knight instead, shrinking it to 1/1 so Skulk lets it slip past every blocker, adding 1 more damage to the 6 from Unmaking, hitting exactly 7 for lethal. I want to verify the layers carefully: Gideon's +1 turns him into a 5/5 indestructible creature-planeswalker, the emblem bumps him to 6/6, and casting Wrappings resets his base power/toughness before the emblem re-applies on top.

Gideon has been under continuous control, so no summoning sickness issue. With no blocks possible, once blockers are declared I cast Anguished Unmaking on Illusory Wrappings to exile it, restoring Gideon to 6/6 (losing 3 life is fine since life total doesn't matter). That brings total damage to 6 plus Knight's 1.

Mana works out to 7 total: I need blue and white from the Farmlands, black from Swamps for both Dead Weight and Unmaking, with the rest as generic — using 4 Farmland and 3 Swamp covers everything. I'm also considering whether targeting Dead Weight instead with Unmaking might be simpler for the Knight.

The removal on Illusory Wrappings actually deals more damage than expected since it turns off the exile clause, bringing damage to 7 total, exactly lethal. The opponent has no instant-speed responses to disrupt this, and blocking isn't a factor either way, so the plan holds up cleanly.

The sequencing needs to be right: Gideon's +1 and casting Wrappings both happen at sorcery speed in the main phase, along with Dead Weight on the Knight, before moving to combat and using Anguished Unmaking on the Wrappings once no blocks are declared.
